chunks: Ibn Nuh said: My grandfather Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Abbas ibn Nuh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me saying: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn Ismail ibn Salih al-Saymari narrated to me saying:

When Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him, sent the epistle (Tawqi') cursing Ibn Abi Azaqir, he sent it from his prison in the house of al-Muqtadir to our Shaykh, Abu Ali ibn Hammam, may Allah have mercy on him, in Dhul-Hijjah of the year 312 AH. Abu Ali, may Allah have mercy on him, dictated it to me and informed me that Abu al-Qasim had suggested to the Imam not to make it public, for he was in the hands of the people and in their prison. So he was ordered to disclose it and not to fear, and he would be safe. Thus he was freed and exited from prison after a short while, and praise be to Allah.

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي الْعَزَاقِرِ: A specific individual cursed by the Imam
key_terms.التَّوْقِيع: Epistle or letter issued by the Imam
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ أَبُو الْقَاسِمُ: Refers to al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a key deputy of the Imam
key_terms.دَارُ الْمُقْتَدِر: The residence/prison of the Abbasid Caliph al-Muqtadir

ai.seo_question: What is the story behind the Imam's epistle cursing Ibn Abi Azaqir and how was it transmitted?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the transmission of a specific *Tawqi'* (epistle) from Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) cursing Ibn Abi Azaqir, highlighting the political dynamics of the Minor Occultation. It illustrates the strategic caution of the Four Deputies, particularly Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, who initially concealed the decree to avoid Abbasid persecution before publicly displaying it once the risk subsided, thereby affirming the Imam's authority through his representatives.
